M1_canonical_density_summary.description: Canonical per-iteration p=0.5 density across 21 task-definition pairs
M1_canonical_density_summary.summary: Near-zero densities consistent with prior experiments (EXP-INTEL-35353016702 mean 0.006). Low variance reflects p=0.5 independent inclusion on sparse locatable_sample.

M2_weighted_density_summary.summary: High mean because DEF-FULL-MAP matches all 20 elements (density=1.0 for 7/21 pairs). DEF-FORM-ONLY also high (17-19/20 elements match). Only ISOLATED-A-LINK produces low density (1-3 elements).

M3_hierarchy_density_summary.summary: Mean identical to weighted density because depth estimation based on inForm flag produces identical weight distributions across tasks. The hierarchy recipe is a monotonic transformation of weighted, not a structurally different recipe.

M4_C1_hierarchy_variation.description: C1: CV of hierarchy-weighted density across 21 pairs
M4_C1_hierarchy_variation.summary: C1 passes: CV=0.58 >> 0.10 threshold. The hierarchy recipe varies across task-definition pairs, primarily driven by definition choice (DEF-FULL-MAP vs ISOLATED-A-LINK).

M5_C2_outside_convex_hull.description: C2: Count of pairs with hierarchy_density outside [min(canonical, weighted), max(canonical, weighted)]
M5_C2_outside_convex_hull.summary: C2 passes: 7/21 pairs have hierarchy_density ABOVE the convex hull. All7 are ISOLATED-A-LINK pairs where hierarchy density (0.088-0.210) exceeds weighted density (0.005-0.019). The hull-breaking occurs because hierarchy upweights shallow non-form elements (nav links, action buttons) that have minimal area in the weighted recipe.

M6_C3_not_linear_combination.description: C3: Spearman correlation of hierarchy with canonical and weighted densities
M6_C3_not_linear_combination.summary: C3 passes (barely): |rho(hier, canonical)|=0.879 < 0.90 threshold. However, |rho(hier, weighted)|=1.0 exactly — the hierarchy recipe produces a PERFECT monotonic transformation of weighted density. This is not 'different from a linear combination' in any meaningful sense; it is a reparameterization.

M7_C4_task_type_structure.description: C4: eta-squared of hierarchy-density on page_type
M7_C4_task_type_structure.summary: C4 decisively FAILS: eta^2=0.000. The hierarchy-weighted density has IDENTICAL mean across all three page types (listing=detail=cart=0.667). This is because: (a) the depth estimation is based on inForm which is binary, not structural; (b) all 20 locatable_sample elements have identical element composition across tasks; (c) the depth distribution is the same for all tasks within each definition.

M8_verdict.rule_triggered: C1 AND C2 AND C3 AND NOT C4 => FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (C4 failure: zero task-type structure)

M9_PC1_hierarchy_variation.description: Positive control: hierarchy density differs across page types with inter-type ratio > 1.1
M9_PC1_hierarchy_variation.summary: PC1 fails: all three page types have identical mean hierarchy density (0.667). The depth estimation (based on inForm flag) is invariant to page-type-specific DOM structure.

M10_NC1_random_weights.description: Null control: random-weight density shows less structure than hierarchy
M10_NC1_random_weights.summary: NC1 fails: random weights show nearly identical correlation structure to hierarchy weights (mean|rho(rand,canon)|=0.877 vs |rho(hier,canon)|=0.879). The hierarchy recipe does not produce more systematic structure than random weights.

M11_alpha_sensitivity.description: Sensitivity of results to alpha parameter (depth decay rate)
M11_alpha_sensitivity.summary: Eta-squared is 0.0 at ALL alpha values. Task-type structure is absent regardless of depth decay rate. The number of hull-breaking pairs varies (10, 7, 13) but all hull breaks are ISOLATED-A-LINK pairs above the hull.

M12_baseline_comparison.description: Comparison with B3 linear mean baseline
M12_baseline_comparison.summary: Linear mean (B3) has rho(canonical)=0.895 and rho(weighted)=0.984, and produces 0 hull breaks (by mathematical identity). Hierarchy has rho(canonical)=0.879 (slightly lower, marginally better) but rho(weighted)=1.0 (identical, no improvement). The hierarchy recipe adds one new dimension (ISOLATED-A-LINK hull breaks) but provides zero task-type discrimination.

M13_recipe_identity.description: Root cause: hierarchy recipe is isomorphic to weighted recipe
M13_recipe_identity.mechanism: The depth estimation heuristic assigns depth based on inForm (binary), not actual DOM tree structure. Since ALL locatable_sample elements have the same inForm pattern across tasks, the depth distribution is task-invariant. The hierarchy recipe therefore produces a MONOTONIC transformation of weighted density (Spearman rho=1.0) that preserves rank ordering while shifting absolute values for ISOLATED-A-LINK pairs.
M13_recipe_identity.evidence: Spearman(hierarchy, weighted)=1.0 at alpha=0.3. All type_means=0.667 (identical). Eta-squared=0.0 at all alpha values.

B1_CANONICAL_RECIPE.observed: Canonical mean=0.00517, range [0.00041, 0.00935]. Consistent with prior experiments.

B2_WEIGHTED_RECIPE.observed: Weighted mean=0.667, range [0.00469, 1.0]. DEF-FULL-MAP=1.0, DEF-FORM-ONLY~0.99, ISOLATED-A-LINK~0.005-0.019.

B3_LINEAR_MEAN.expected: Always ranks between canonical and weighted (0 hull breaks)
B3_LINEAR_MEAN.observed: 0 hull breaks, rho(canonical)=0.895, rho(weighted)=0.984. Confirmed degenerate.

B4_DENSITY_RATIO.observed: Not directly recomputed in this experiment; parent results (EXP-INTEL-35375593989) confirm R is definition-driven.

PC1_HIERARCHY_VARIATION.description: DOM hierarchy depth varies across page types — hierarchy density should differ
PC1_HIERARCHY_VARIATION.observed: All three types have identical mean (0.667). Inter-type ratio=1.0. FAIL.

NC1_RANDOM_WEIGHTS.description: Random-weight density should show less structure than hierarchy
NC1_RANDOM_WEIGHTS.observed: Random mean|rho(canonical)|=0.877, mean|rho(weighted)|=0.978. Both exceed 0.30. FAIL.

observations.description: The hierarchy-weighted density recipe (exp(-alpha * depth) weighting with alpha=0.3) produces density values that are a PERFECT monotonic transformation of the weighted recipe (Spearman rho=1.0). The hierarchy recipe does not introduce a structurally different ranking; it reparameterizes the existing weighted ranking.

The hierarchy recipe breaks the convex hull on 7/21 pairs (all ISOLATED-A-LINK), with all7 hull breaks ABOVE the hull (hierarchy > weighted). This occurs because hierarchy upweights shallow non-form elements (depth=1-2, nav links, action buttons) that have minimal area in the weighted recipe but receive equal weight in the hierarchy recipe.

The hierarchy-weighted density has IDENTICAL mean across all three page types (listing=detail=cart=0.667). Eta-squared=0.0 at all alpha values (0.1, 0.3, 0.5). The depth estimation heuristic (based on inForm binary flag) is invariant to page-type-specific DOM structure.

The random-weight null control shows nearly identical correlation structure to hierarchy weights (mean|rho(rand,canon)|=0.877 vs |rho(hier,canon)|=0.879). The hierarchy recipe does not produce more systematic structure than random weights, confirming it is not a meaningful structural recipe.

Root cause: The depth estimation heuristic uses inForm (a binary attribute) as the primary depth proxy. Since the locatable_sample contains a fixed set of 20 elements per task with the same inForm distribution across all tasks, the depth distribution is task-invariant. The hierarchy recipe therefore cannot differentiate task types.

The convex hull breaks occur only for ISOLATED-A-LINK (the most restrictive definition, 1-3 matching elements). For DEF-FULL-MAP (20 matching elements) and DEF-FORM-ONLY (17-19 matching elements), hierarchy density is always between canonical and weighted. The hull-breaking is definition-dependent, not task-type-dependent.

validity_notes.note: The depth estimation is a HEURISTIC, not actual DOM tree depth. The locatable_sample is a flattened list without parent-child links. Depth is inferred from tag type and inForm flag, which provides at most 4 distinct depth levels. True DOM tree depth could range from 2 to 20+ levels.

Results are bounded to truncated-first-20 locatable_sample (7 tasks, 1 Magento site, 3 definitions). The fixed sample size (20 elements per task) means all tasks have identical element count, eliminating any depth-distribution variation that might arise from different DOM sizes.

The hierarchy recipe's perfect correlation with weighted (rho=1.0) at alpha=0.3 suggests the depth estimation is effectively a reparameterization of area-based weighting. At alpha=0.1 and alpha=0.5, the correlation is slightly lower (0.95, 0.94) but still very high, and eta-squared remains 0.0 at all alpha values.

The experiment does not test whether TRUE DOM hierarchy depth (from complete DOM tree, not flattened locatable_sample) would produce different results. The negative result applies to the heuristic depth estimation, not to the theoretical possibility that genuine DOM depth information could break the degeneracy.

The NC1 null control fails because random weights on the same 20-element locatable_sample produce similar correlation structure to hierarchy weights. This is expected when depth estimation is binary (inForm) — random [0,1] weights on a fixed set of 20 elements naturally produce similar rank-ordering patterns.

unresolved.question: Would TRUE DOM hierarchy depth (from complete DOM tree with parent-child links, not the flattened locatable_sample) produce a structurally different recipe that breaks the convex hull AND captures task-type structure?
unresolved.blocked_by: Requires access to complete DOM tree structure (not available in locatable_sample)

unresolved.question: Given that linear combinations, density ratios, and DOM hierarchy weighting all fail to produce a viable MIXED decision rule, should the MIXED outcome program be abandoned entirely?
unresolved.blocked_by: Requires product lane decision on MIXED handling strategy

unresolved.question: Could a fundamentally different metric (e.g., semantic role weighting, conditional inclusion based on element relationships, or a learned embedding) produce rankings that are both outside the convex hull AND capture task-type structure?
unresolved.blocked_by: Requires testing with genuinely structural element representations beyond the flattened locatable_sample
